# SQL source syntax and scanner qualification

The baseline is the published `tree-sitter-sequel` 0.3.11 archive, SHA-256
`9d198ad3c319c02e43c21efa1ec796b837afcb96ffaef1a40c1978fbdcec7d17`.
Its VCS metadata names `7b51ecda191d36b92f5a90a8d1bc3faef1c7b8b8` with a dirty
checkout. The published grammar, build script and highlight query match that
commit. The omitted MIT license is restored verbatim from the same commit.
Tree-sitter CLI 0.24.7 with ABI 14 reproduced the published parser, grammar JSON
and node types byte for byte before local syntax changes. The exact published
grammar and six generated source files remain alongside the active inputs with
an `.orig` suffix; their independent hashes are recorded in `grammars.lock`.

The preferred grammar adds typed, written T-SQL procedure headers, physical
parameters and scalar/table declarations, bracket-delimited raw identifiers,
MAX type arguments and IDENTITY column clauses. Procedure bodies admit a
bounded supported statement grammar: explicit BEGIN/END blocks or one unbraced
statement. An explicit script envelope adds physical GO batch boundaries,
written SET option ON/OFF statements and closed IF/ELSE BEGIN/END branches.
Its non-routine batches admit only those SET options, closed conditionals,
CREATE TABLE and DECLARE statements. Standalone SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE,
RETURN and SET ... TO followed by GO remain outside this partial batch slice;
their existing ordinary SQL or procedure-body productions are not broadened.
GO is a contextual native token, never global whitespace; ordinary SQL retains
its original semicolon rules. Procedure batches admit only the bounded routine
body, not an arbitrary following statement list. Unsupported routine execution
and control flow remain parse gaps. This slice does not establish complete
T-SQL syntax, condition evaluation, batch execution or catalog semantics.
Bracket syntax must preserve the existing PostgreSQL array and dollar-function
contracts. Ambiguous implicit bracket aliases do not establish a dialect-specific
interpretation. Malformed headers, missing delimiters and recovered procedure errors
cannot establish valid declaration owners in the structural adapter. Recovered
or incomplete conditional branches likewise cannot establish child owners.

Table keys admit written CLUSTERED/NONCLUSTERED modifiers and key-local WITH
options: explicit boolean settings or FILLFACTOR integer syntax, including the
legacy unparenthesized FILLFACTOR form. These settings remain attached to the
column or table key, not the table's storage options. They do not validate SQL
Server option compatibility or numeric ranges. Unnamed UNIQUE WITH options
and other index settings remain outside this slice.

Shared SQL statements retain both ordinary-program and explicit-batch
interpretations until their enclosing boundaries disambiguate them. The six
additional conflicts correspond to generator-reported overlapping productions;
no global precedence discards an existing dialect interpretation.

The active static tables are regenerated from the reviewed preferred grammar
using the pinned local Tree-sitter CLI 0.24.4, Node.js 24.11.1 and ABI 14. Two
independent preparations must produce identical generated bytes. Cargo consumes
only those checked-in native inputs; it neither invokes the generator nor
fetches sources. This preparation does not reproduce the original upstream
tables and does not prove an independently network-blocked, empty-cache build.

The six active derived inputs matched byte for byte across two independent
preparations. The generated action and native state indices fit their ABI 14
storage widths, including the uint16_t parse-table entries: maximum action
index 55138 and maximum state index 33693. This numeric ABI validation does not
establish language completeness or runtime performance. The local native
regression run passed all 7 scanner-state, 5 ordinary SQL syntax and 18 T-SQL
syntax tests. These source-syntax tests do not establish fresh corpus coverage,
whole-language semantics, installed MCP behavior or indexing performance.

The scanner retains complete UTF-8 dollar delimiters in fixed-capacity state.
Snapshots have a version byte, a little-endian two-byte length and the exact
delimiter bytes. Empty state has zero serialized bytes. Only complete tags
that fit the existing 1024-byte native ABI frame can enter persistent state;
oversized tokens fail without mutating prior context. Malformed frames reset
the state instead of retaining a partial tag or an unchecked C string.

Serialization does not consume live context. Deserialization and scanning do
not allocate per delimiter; allocation failure at construction fails closed.
Literal scanning preserves overlapping dollar prefixes, embedded NUL body
bytes and case-sensitive Unicode delimiters. It leaves the enclosing function
delimiter intact when scanning a differently tagged literal.

The three dollar token ordinals and their serialized state format are preserved.
The appended GO token is stateless and requires a physical line containing only
optional spaces/tabs, GO, an optional positive decimal count and an optional
line comment. LF, CRLF and EOF boundaries are supported; counts are retained as
source syntax and never evaluated or executed. Same-line statements, zero or
negative counts, identifier prefixes and semicolon suffixes are not boundaries.
Block comments on the GO utility line remain unsupported rather than being
silently accepted as trivia. GO-like bytes in dollar literals do not change
scanner state or become batch tokens.

The grammar's permissive punctuation tags are preserved. This scanner bounds
source tokens, not SQL dialect validity or database name resolution. The native
state and syntax regression suites live in `tests/native-grammars`; SQL text is
never executed by these tests. This package alone is not a structural adapter
or evidence of complete SQL semantic coverage.
